nodes.title: Facility location
nodes.summary: Choose facilities and connect demand points under cost, distance, capacity, or coverage requirements.

nodes.title: Uncapacitated facility location (UFLP)
nodes.summary: Pay opening costs and serve every customer without binding facility capacity.

nodes.title: Single-source capacitated facility location (SSCFLP)
nodes.summary: Open capacitated facilities and assign each indivisible customer to exactly one open facility.

nodes.title: p-median
nodes.summary: Open exactly p facilities and minimize total demand-weighted assignment distance.

nodes.title: Canonical UFLP model
nodes.summary: Use binary open y_i and assignment x_ij; select the x domain from splittable versus indivisible service semantics.

payload.objective: min sum(i in I, f[i]*y[i]) + sum((i,j) in A, c[i,j]*x[i,j])
constraints: sum(i in I_j, x[i,j]) == 1 for j in J
payload.decision_gate: Use binary x only for indivisible single-source assignment; continuous [0,1] may represent fractional service.

nodes.title: Canonical SSCFLP model
nodes.summary: Binary open and assignment variables with exact-one assignment, open-linking, and aggregate demand-weighted capacity.

variables: y[i] binary: facility i is open
x[i,j] binary: customer j is assigned to facility i
payload.objective: min sum(i in I, f[i]*y[i]) + sum((i,j) in A, c[i,j]*x[i,j])
constraints: sum(i in I_j, x[i,j]) == 1 for j in J
sum(j in J_i, demand[j]*x[i,j]) <= capacity[i]*y[i] for i in I

nodes.title: Canonical p-median model
nodes.summary: Open exactly p sites, assign each demand point once, and minimize demand-weighted distance.

constraints: sum(i in I_j, x[i,j]) == 1 for j in J

nodes.title: Retail depots with fixed cost and no capacity
nodes.summary: Candidate depots have opening and customer-service costs; depot capacity is explicitly unlimited.

payload.reuse_rule: Do not invent capacity merely because the entities are warehouses or depots.

nodes.title: Capacitated warehouses with indivisible customers
nodes.summary: Open warehouses with fixed costs and capacity; assign each customer's full demand to exactly one warehouse.

payload.reuse_rule: Indivisibility determines binary x; capacity consumes demand[j], not customer count.

nodes.title: Choose exactly p emergency stations
nodes.summary: Choose exactly p stations and minimize population-weighted travel distance.

payload.reuse_rule: Facility count is a hard equality; do not replace it with fixed opening costs.

nodes.title: Assignment is not linked to opening
nodes.summary: Customers can be assigned to a closed facility because x[i,j] <= y[i] or an equivalent implication is missing.

nodes.title: Assignment domain contradicts semantics
nodes.summary: Continuous x permits forbidden splitting, or binary x creates an unnecessary MILP when splitting is allowed.

nodes.title: Capacity counts customers instead of demand
nodes.summary: sum_j x[i,j] <= capacity[i] is dimensionally wrong when customer demands vary.

nodes.title: Closed facilities retain capacity
nodes.summary: The capacity right-hand side omits y[i], so a closed facility may still serve demand.

nodes.title: Customers are optional or multiply assigned
nodes.summary: Using <=1 or >=1 instead of equality changes exact-one service semantics.

nodes.title: p-median and fixed-charge location are confused
nodes.summary: An exact-p rule is replaced with opening costs, or an arbitrary p is invented.

payload.symptom: facility count follows the wrong decision rule

nodes.title: Add an opening link
nodes.summary: Add x[i,j] <= y[i] for every feasible pair unless another proven constraint already gives the implication.

nodes.title: Choose x from service semantics
nodes.summary: Use binary x for indivisible exact-one assignment and continuous flow only when splitting is allowed.

nodes.title: Use demand-weighted, opening-gated capacity
nodes.summary: Use sum_j demand[j]*x[i,j] <= capacity[i]*y[i] after confirming compatible units.

nodes.title: Enforce exact-one assignment
nodes.summary: Use sum_i x[i,j] == 1 for every required customer over feasible arcs.

nodes.title: Represent the facility-count rule
nodes.summary: For p-median use sum_i y[i] == p; for fixed-charge location do not invent that equality.

nodes.title: Closed-site service check
nodes.summary: For each y[i]=0, recompute total assigned service and require zero.

nodes.title: Customer assignment check
nodes.summary: Recompute sum_i x[i,j] and require exactly one for each single-source customer.

nodes.title: Capacity and units check
nodes.summary: Recompute demand-weighted load and confirm both sides use the same unit.

nodes.title: Facility-count check
nodes.summary: For p-median, recompute sum_i y[i] and require exactly p.
